articles.title: 'Patriot' passports with Trump's image expanding across US
articles.summary: The State Department announced it is expanding availability of a new commemorative U.S. passport featuring President Trump's image, making an additional 250,000 copies available in response to public demand.

articles.title: 15-year-old convicted murderer sentenced to 100 years in prison
articles.summary: Jo'Majze Larry, a 15-year-old, was convicted of murder by an Indiana jury in June and has been sentenced to 100 years in prison.

articles.title: A Lose-Lose for Food Stamps
articles.summary: A looming deadline may force some states to end SNAP (food stamp) benefits next year, creating a difficult situation for both states and recipients. The story matters because it highlights policy challenges affecting food security for millions of Americans.

articles.title: ACLU of Iowa Report Finds Police in Schools Led to Harsher Discipline for Minor Offenses, Disparate Enforcement
articles.summary: An ACLU of Iowa report finds that police presence in schools led to harsher discipline for minor offenses and disparate enforcement. The report documents impacts of school-based policing on student discipline practices.

articles.title: Activists climb rare Arizona cottonwood to shield it from Trump border wall construction
articles.summary: Activists are protesting Trump border wall construction in Arizona because it would require removing an ancient Fremont cottonwood tree estimated to be 200-250 years old; a demonstrator was arrested Wednesday for trespassing during the protest.

articles.title: Andy Burnham to give regional mayors share of income tax
articles.summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham plans to give regional mayors a share of income tax revenue to decentralize power across the country. Critics argue the proposal lacks sufficient detail.

articles.title: At least 50 NYC kids shot in gun crimes so far this year – including tragic 12-year-old boy
articles.summary: NYPD data shows that 49 youth under 18 were victims of shootings in NYC during the first half of 2026, with a 12-year-old among the casualties. The statistics highlight a significant problem of gun violence affecting children in the city.

articles.title: Carville says one democratic socialist's 'lunacy of the highest level' policy could haunt swing state Dems
articles.summary: James Carville warns that democratic socialist candidates in Michigan and Wisconsin Democratic primaries could damage the national Democratic Party's image. The comment reflects concerns about how primary candidates might affect swing state Democrats in general elections.

articles.title: Cornyn and Tillis meet with Blanche amid hold on attorney general nomination
articles.summary: Todd Blanche's attorney general nomination is delayed as Republican senators John Cornyn and Thom Tillis intend to vote against his confirmation. The two senators are meeting with Blanche amid the hold on his nomination.

articles.title: Democratic, Republican strategists unpack stalled Blanche nomination, Michigan Senate race and more

articles.title: Dozens of sex workers and their johns busted after capitalizing on San Diego Comic-Con: ‘Ugly truth’
articles.summary: A sting operation during San Diego Comic-Con resulted in dozens of arrests of alleged sex buyers and 9 alleged sex workers. The operation was characterized as exposing what authorities describe as the "ugly truth" of illegal activity during the event.

articles.title: Emily Moreno files restraining order against ex-husband Rep. Max Miller
articles.summary: Emily Moreno filed a restraining order against her ex-husband Rep. Max Miller (R-OH), alleging he grabbed her lawyer during an encounter. The restraining order was filed in Cuyahoga County, Ohio.

articles.title: Father who bought AR-15 for Georgia school shooter learns fate in first-of-its-kind conviction
articles.summary: Colin Gray received a 15-year sentence after a jury found he gave his son an AR-15 used in the Apalachee High School shooting despite being aware of mental health warnings. The conviction is described as the first of its kind.

articles.title: Fetterman calls himself the ‘conscience of the Democratic Party’ in meeting with Netanyahu
articles.summary: Senator John Fetterman (D-PA) met with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and described himself as the "conscience of the Democratic Party" for his support of Israel. The two emphasized the close U.S.-Israel partnership.

articles.title: Fox News Poll: GOP divisions shape Texas Senate race
articles.summary: According to a Fox News poll, Republican Ken Paxton trails Democrat James Talarico by three points in the 2026 Texas Senate race, with character concerns and GOP divisions shaping the midterm contest.

articles.title: In Missouri, Cori Bush and Wesley Bell's primary rematch sets up key test for Democrats
articles.summary: Progressive congresswoman Cori Bush, who previously served two terms, faces a primary rematch against Wesley Bell, a moderate local prosecutor who defeated her in a primary challenge. The race sets up a key test for Democrats between progressive and moderate factions.

articles.title: Judge rules Wisconsin voters can't recast ballots after governor race shakeup
articles.summary: A Wisconsin judge ruled that voters cannot request new ballots for the Democratic primary gubernatorial race following recent candidate withdrawals and re-entries, ending a lawsuit by the state's Democratic Party.

articles.title: Liars and Loons
articles.summary: The Dispatch publishes an opinion piece examining Anthony Fauci and a missed populist political opportunity.

articles.title: Mandela Barnes drops out of high-stakes Wisconsin governor’s race
articles.summary: Mandela Barnes, the former lieutenant governor of Wisconsin, dropped out of the Democratic primary for governor less than two weeks before the election, citing that democratic socialist Francesca Hong had surged ahead with a commanding lead and he no longer saw a viable path to the nomination.

articles.title: Maniac who stabbed two while screaming ‘Allahu Akbar’ indicted for NYC hate crime attack: DA
articles.summary: Raul Morales, a 51-year-old accused of stabbing two people while screaming 'Allahu Akbar' on the Upper West Side, was indicted on hate crime charges, prosecutors announced.

articles.title: McCarthy: Pelosi would 'yell' at Republicans that they 'shouldn't be in the room'
articles.summary: Former Speaker Kevin McCarthy said that former Speaker Nancy Pelosi treated Republicans poorly and would sometimes "yell" at GOP lawmakers. McCarthy made the comments while discussing perceptions between conservatives and liberals.

articles.title: Missouri couple murdered in Guatemala after husband was deported
articles.summary: Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche's nomination to lead the Department of Justice full-time is stalled as Republican senators John Cornyn and Thom Tillis oppose it unless the DOJ eliminates a $1.8 billion fund for payments to people who believe they were wrongfully prosecuted. The two senators' demands are holding up the nomination process.

articles.title: New forecast shifts 13 House seats, Georgia Senate race toward Democrats
articles.summary: The University of Virginia's Sabato's Crystal Ball election forecaster has updated its midterm outlook, shifting 13 House seats and the Georgia Senate race toward Democrats.

articles.title: NY Rep. Mike Lawler’s race now a ‘toss-up’ as Dems target battleground district that could flip Congress
articles.summary: An independent analyst has rated New York's 17th House District race between Republican incumbent Mike Lawler and Democrat Cait Conley as a toss-up, signaling the seat could flip control. Democrats are targeting the Hudson Valley swing district as a potential pickup opportunity.

articles.title: Pentagon fires back after Mark Kelly accuses Pete Hegseth of targeting women and Black military officers
articles.summary: The Department of Defense rejected Senator Mark Kelly's claims that Defense Secretary nominee Pete Hegseth targeted women and Black military officers, asserting that promotions are based on merit. The dispute centers on Hegseth's record regarding diversity in military advancement.

articles.title: Politics is getting more vulgar, with two presidents leading the way on curse words counts: study
articles.summary: A study found that 87% of all presidential swear words dating back to 1919 have occurred within the past 10 years, indicating politics is becoming increasingly profane. The research highlights a notable shift in the language used by recent commanders in chief.

articles.title: Poll analysis on cost of living and whether political parties have answers
articles.summary: A CBS News poll found that large majorities of Americans say their incomes are not keeping up with inflation and believe the president is not focused enough on the cost of living issue. The poll highlights public concern about economic pressures and presidential responsiveness on the matter.

articles.title: President Trump pushes lawmakers on legislation as 'Protect College Sports Act' hangs on by a thread
articles.summary: President Trump is pushing lawmakers to pass the 'Protect College Sports Act,' with Senate negotiations stalling over conference realignment caps, tampering penalties, and a $22.5 million retention pool.

articles.title: Rep. Max Miller facing domestic abuse allegations as he runs for reelection
articles.summary: Republican Rep. Max Miller of Ohio faces domestic abuse allegations while running for reelection, which he denies.

articles.title: Rep. Ralph Norman says he expects South Carolina GOP Senate primary to go to runoff amid tight polls
articles.summary: Rep. Ralph Norman, who leads in a tight Emerson College poll for South Carolina's open Senate seat, expects the race to go to a runoff. Norman is ahead of Lindsey Graham's sister Darline in the competition to fill the late senator's seat.

articles.title: Rock-hurling crew stabbed 2 teen boys, snatched electric scooter in NYC attack: cops
articles.summary: Police say a group of seven muggers threw rocks at three teenagers and stabbed two of them during a robbery in Queens, stealing an electric scooter. The attack occurred in Corona near 111th Street and 49th Avenue.

articles.title: Sanders, Grassley reintroduce bill fining Pentagon for audit failures
articles.summary: Senators Bernie Sanders and Chuck Grassley reintroduced a bipartisan bill that would impose financial fines on the Pentagon if the department fails its annual audits. The measure targets the Pentagon's repeated failure to pass financial audits.

articles.title: Schiff-backed candidate abruptly ends gubernatorial campaign amid rumblings of a damaging report
articles.summary: Democratic candidate Mandela Barnes suspended his Wisconsin gubernatorial campaign during the primary race. The suspension occurred amid reports of a potentially damaging report, leaving other candidates as major contenders.

articles.title: Seattle mayor says police chief has resigned after criticism of festival shooting response
articles.summary: Seattle's police chief has resigned following criticism of the city's response to a fatal shooting at a food festival. Mayor Katie Wilson announced the resignation on Thursday.

articles.title: Seattle police chief resigns after deadly food festival shooting
articles.summary: Seattle Police Chief Shon Barnes resigned following criticism of the city's response to a fatal shooting at a food festival the previous weekend. The resignation came after the mayor publicly called for his departure.

articles.title: Senate 'YOLO Caucus' bucks Trump on Blanche: What to know

articles.title: Sneaky new teachers’ union plan to indoctrinate our kids: classroom AI
articles.summary: The New York Post opinion piece argues that teachers' unions plan to use classroom AI as a tool for indoctrination rather than education. The article presents this as a strategic concern about how AI will be deployed in schools.

articles.title: Steve Bannon predicts Todd Blanche fight could be final straw for Trump’s relationship with Thune
articles.summary: Steve Bannon predicts that President Trump's strained relationship with Senate Majority Leader John Thune could reach a breaking point over the nomination of acting Attorney General Todd Blanche. Bannon, a Trump ally, suggests this dispute may be the final catalyst for irreparable damage between the two.

articles.title: The distant date that Mamdani has chosen for his city-owned grocery stores should raise alarm bells
articles.summary: An opinion column suggests that New York official Mamdani has set a distant 2029 timeline for implementing city-owned grocery stores, with the author arguing this delay is strategically timed to occur after the next election. The piece implies the official may be using a delayed implementation date to avoid accountability.

articles.title: This Is What It Looks Like When Senate Republicans Have Nothing Left to Lose
articles.summary: According to Slate, Senate Republicans have shifted their approach after Trump's actions against certain lawmakers. The article suggests this has paradoxically given these Republicans more political freedom to act independently.

articles.title: Trump Education Department probes school after teacher allegedly required same-sex students to kiss
articles.summary: The Trump administration opened a federal investigation into Denver Public Schools after allegations that a teacher required same-sex students to kiss in class.

articles.title: Trump says he might pull Todd Blanche's AG nomination until Cornyn and Tillis leave office
articles.summary: President Trump threatened on Thursday to temporarily pull Todd Blanche's nomination for attorney general amid opposition from Republican Senators John Cornyn and Thom Tillis.

articles.title: Trump ‘not sure’ he will let Ukraine build Patriot missiles
articles.summary: President Trump stated he is 'not sure' whether he will permit Ukraine to manufacture Patriot missiles, reversing an earlier position where he said he would allow such production. Patriot missiles are considered vital to Ukraine's defense against Russia.

articles.title: Trump's CDC, ASPR nominees advance out of Senate committee
articles.summary: The Senate HELP Committee voted 12-10 to advance two of President Trump's health nominees for the CDC and ASPR to a full Senate vote.

articles.title: Trump-aligned parents rally behind kids' online safety rules
articles.summary: Conservative parents' rights groups are pushing Senate leaders to preserve a "duty of care" provision in an online safety bill and increase tech company protections for children. The groups are rallying behind the legislation as it moves through Congress.

articles.title: Turek declines to say he'd back Schumer
articles.summary: Iowa state Rep. Josh Turek (D) declined to answer whether he would support Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) for Democratic leadership in the next Congress during a Wednesday interview. The question arose as midterm elections approach.

articles.title: Video shows 200 migrant children at California container site during Xavier Becerra’s HHS tenure
articles.summary: A campaign features video showing 200 migrant children at a California container site during Xavier Becerra's tenure as HHS secretary, citing whistleblower allegations that he ignored concerns about unaccompanied migrant children placements. The claims are part of campaign messaging that also includes a new website seeking tips.

articles.title: Washington school district reviewing incident of employee making celebratory remark about Charlie Kirk's death
articles.summary: The Lake Washington School District launched a review after a viral video showed a staff member apparently making a celebratory remark about Charlie Kirk's death. The district is investigating the incident involving the political commentator.

articles.title: Why Trump’s attorney general nominee is struggling
articles.summary: Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche, whom Trump nominated for the permanent position last month, is facing difficulties with his confirmation process. The article does not provide specific details about the nature of his struggles.

The result represents a 22-point margin of support for such an arrest.

articles.title: As Spain battles wildfires, its politicians battle over climate change's role
articles.summary: Spain is battling wildfires that have burned nearly 200,000 acres, with another round of extreme heat expected to exceed 100 degrees Fahrenheit starting Wednesday. Politicians are debating the role of climate change in the fires.

articles.title: Burma approves death penalty for scammers months after FBI's $8 billion crypto crackdown
articles.summary: Burma enacted a new law imposing the death penalty for internet scammers, following months after the FBI's seizure of $8 billion in Bitcoin from a criminal network. The timing reflects increasing global attention to cybercrime enforcement.

articles.title: California couple flee monster wildfire in France — a year after home was destroyed by Eaton Fire
articles.summary: An Altadena couple who lost their home in last year's Eaton Fire fled from Bordeaux, France to Paris after wildfires erupted in the region. The family is experiencing a second displacement from major fire events within a year.

articles.title: California is home to some of the most dangerous cities in US — Bay Area near bottom of safety ranking
articles.summary: San Francisco and Oakland rank among the 10 least safe cities in the US, with Oakland recording a crime rate of 19.3 per 1,000 residents, second only to Memphis.

articles.title: Criminal gangs increasingly lure victims to work in online scam centers, UN migration agency warns
articles.summary: A UN migration agency warns that criminal gangs are increasingly luring victims to work in online scam centers, where they are held captive, have documents seized, and are forced through violence and threats to participate in scams.

articles.title: Deadly French wildfires threaten missile plants, nuclear sites as fourth heatwave looms
articles.summary: Wildfires in France have scorched over 104,000 acres and are threatening evacuation of missile factories and nuclear research sites near Bordeaux as a fourth heatwave approaches.

articles.title: Even in death, Lindsey Graham  is driving diplomacy forward

articles.title: Grenada officials reexamining missing American woman's last known movements

articles.title: Grieving mum was told baby's ashes were animal remains
articles.summary: A mother says she was mistakenly told her baby's ashes were animal remains. The incident has left her uncertain about her child's actual remains.

articles.title: Houthis Claim Strike on Another Saudi Oil Tanker
articles.summary: The Houthi group in Yemen claims to have struck another Saudi oil tanker in the Red Sea as part of an escalating blockade of Saudi shipping in the vital waterway. The group is operating with Iranian support amid broader tensions in the region.

articles.title: How Mexican drug cartels have outsourced meth labs to Nigeria
articles.summary: Mexican drug cartels are outsourcing methamphetamine production to Nigeria, as West Africa becomes an increasingly attractive location for manufacturing and exporting illicit drugs.

articles.title: Iran Considered Retaliatory Strike on Ukrainian Seaport
articles.summary: Iran considered launching a retaliatory strike on a Ukrainian seaport in an incident that risked escalating into a wider conflict, according to officials, though diplomatic efforts have since eased tensions. The situation highlighted the fragile state of regional security.

articles.title: Iran fires missiles at US forces in Jordan, ending brief lull in attacks
articles.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps launched multiple ballistic missiles at a base housing US forces in Jordan, ending a pause in attacks that had begun Friday. The strike indicates a renewal of hostilities between Iran and US forces in the region.

articles.title: Iran Hangs Protesters as Executions Surge, Rights Groups Say
articles.summary: According to human rights activists, the Iranian government has been rapidly escalating executions of protesters, with videos appearing to show recent public demonstrations in response.

articles.title: Iran has struck 14 Middle Eastern nations. Here’s what they have at stake in the war
articles.summary: Iran has conducted missile and drone attacks against at least 14 Middle Eastern nations since the U.S. and Israel initially struck Iran, drawing countries beyond the original conflict parties into the war that began in February.

articles.title: Iran launched multiple missiles at American forces, U.S. military says
articles.summary: Iran launched multiple missiles at American forces, and U.S. Central Command said all missiles were successfully intercepted.

articles.title: Iran launches 'surprise attack' on US forces in Middle East
articles.summary: Iran fired multiple ballistic missiles at a US base in the Middle East in what US Central Command called an attempted surprise attack, marking the first publicly disclosed Iranian attack on US service members since President Trump ordered a halt on such attacks last week. The incident signals a resumption of hostilities in the region.

articles.title: Iran says it seeks ‘restitution’ from Ukraine, not escalation, after ship attack
articles.summary: Iran said it seeks "restitution" from Ukraine following a Ukrainian drone strike against an Iranian civilian vessel in the Caspian Sea, with both sides' rhetoric moderating after escalatory statements the previous day. Ukraine's President Zelensky confirmed the country carried out the long-range drone strikes.

articles.title: Japan mall rebuilt after deadly 2016 earthquake destroyed in major temblor weeks after 'fresh start' reopening
articles.summary: An explosion destroyed Aeon Mall in Kumamoto, Japan just weeks after the facility reopened following its reconstruction from a 2016 earthquake, with up to 30 employees unaccounted for.

articles.title: Japan Quake May Weigh on Shares Including Aeon, Nippon Paper
articles.summary: A magnitude 7.1 earthquake in Japan's southwestern Kyushu island killed at least five people and may pressure stocks of companies operating in the region, including Aeon and Nippon Paper.

articles.title: Kushner, Witkoff visit to Ukraine under discussion
articles.summary: Trump officials Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are in discussions about visiting Ukraine to revive U.S. peace negotiations aimed at ending Russia's war, following a Trump-Zelensky meeting, according to Ukrainian officials.

articles.title: Mediators see progress in Iran war ceasefire restoration push
articles.summary: Mediators led by Qatar and Pakistan report progress in U.S.-Iran ceasefire negotiations after both sides paused attacks, with discussions continuing toward an interim ceasefire deal.

articles.title: Nicaragua is officially a dictatorship — and US money paved the way
articles.summary: Nicaraguan leader Daniel Ortega announced the country will never hold elections again, effectively establishing what the article characterizes as an official dictatorship. According to the article, US money has sustained Ortega's government.

articles.title: Pack of coyotes takes over abandoned West Hollywood complex, locals plead for help as apex predators roam streets
articles.summary: A pack of coyotes has taken over an abandoned West Hollywood complex, with local residents requesting help as the apex predators roam nearby streets. The situation has drawn comparisons to the children's book 'Where the Wild Things Are.'

articles.title: Pentagon ties new casualty category for renewed U.S.-Iran fighting to end of 'Operation Epic Fury'
articles.summary: The Pentagon created a new casualty category in its official system to account for those killed and wounded in U.S.-Iran combat operations, coinciding with the announced end of what the military calls 'Operation Epic Fury.'

articles.title: Powerful tornado leaves widespread damage in Wisconsin but time of day may have saved lives
articles.summary: A powerful tornado in northeastern Wisconsin caused widespread damage and remained on the ground for over 20 minutes, with first responders searching for possible victims. The timing of the tornado may have limited casualties.

articles.title: Shootout that killed 3 at festival in Seattle possibly gang-related, investigators say
articles.summary: A shootout at a crowded food festival near Seattle's Space Needle over the weekend killed three people, with investigators saying the violence was possibly gang-related and involving at least three suspects, one of whom was killed. Police announced the preliminary findings on Monday.

articles.title: Spanish firefighters describe how 'alarming' blaze is forcing them to change tactics
articles.summary: Spain's largest recorded wildfire is forcing firefighters to change their approach, shifting focus toward evacuations and property protection due to the fire's severity. The ferocity of the blaze has made traditional firefighting tactics less viable.

articles.title: The Chinese Hand in American Climate Advocacy

articles.title: The Reddit Posts That Surfaced After A Michigan Family Tragedy

articles.title: Torrent of water floods the streets of Los Angeles again — as another sinkhole opens up
articles.summary: A fourth water main break in less than two weeks has flooded Los Angeles streets and opened a sinkhole in the Fairfax District. The repeated infrastructure failures highlight ongoing water system issues in the city.

articles.title: Trump hosts separate meetings with Netanyahu, Zelenskyy
articles.summary: President Trump held separate face-to-face meetings with Ukrainian President Zelenskyy and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu on Tuesday, marking Trump's first in-person meeting with Netanyahu since the start of the Iran conflict.

articles.title: Trump meets Ukrainian, Israeli leaders as they pay respects to Lindsey Graham
articles.summary: President Trump held talks with Ukrainian and Israeli leaders during Senator Lindsey Graham's funeral in Washington. The meetings provided an opportunity for the two countries to engage with Trump on the sidelines of the formal proceedings.

articles.title: Trump meets with Netanyahu for first time since Iran war began
articles.summary: President Trump held separate meetings with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Tuesday. The meetings come amid ongoing tensions in the Middle East and Eastern Europe.

articles.title: Trump meets with Netanyahu, Zelenskyy at White House ahead of Graham funeral
articles.summary: President Trump met with Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu and Ukrainian President Zelenskyy at the White House to discuss foreign policy issues ahead of Sen. Graham's funeral.

articles.summary: The U.S. is planning to increase anti-China spending worldwide by hundreds of millions of dollars, with programs designed to 'reclaim diplomatic leverage' in areas where American funding had previously been reduced.

articles.summary: The U.S. says it intercepted an Iranian missile attack, ending a days-long pause in direct air strikes. The incident marks a resumption of military tensions between the two countries.

articles.summary: Ukrainian President Zelensky and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu met with Trump in Washington while attending Senator Lindsey Graham's funeral, as conflicts continue in Ukraine and Iran.

articles.summary: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu are converging on Washington to meet with Trump, whose support is critical for their respective governments amid ongoing conflicts. articles.summary: The article provides tips and tricks to reduce eye strain and optimize smartphones for extended reading sessions. This matters for the growing number of people consuming long-form content on mobile devices.

articles.summary: Apple is planning to unveil its first smart glasses at WWDC in June 2025, with a launch expected by end of 2027, prioritizing privacy features to differentiate from competitors like Meta. The privacy-focused approach may be contributing to the delayed timeline.

articles.summary: Cornerstone University's president is positioning the institution to develop graduates with irreplaceable human qualities like wisdom that AI cannot replicate. The strategy reflects how higher education is adapting to AI's growing influence.
